reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because its description solicits payment for a crypto academy course and a EUR 19.95 monthly subscription that provides speculative coin information, including coins described as having potential in the next bull run. The PancakeSwap-Google commentary is presented as contextual news rather than the paid offer mechanism.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap and Google are working together.
Would you like to learn everything about cryptocurrencies and blockchain? Then now secure my new crypto course for the complete basic knowledge:
Then join my academy by either buying the crypto course (see link above) or completing a subscription at EUR 19.95 per month (can be canceled at any time) in order to only receive the coin.
Every 1st and every 3. Tuesday of the month I present an exciting coin that has the potential in the next Bullrun.
Would you like to get to know this coin and build your portfolio with it?

opening.argument: The language is conditional and non-guaranteeing rather than a promise of profit. The description calls the featured coin one that has the “potential” to perform in a future bull run, while the speaker says he thinks major players entering crypto will accelerate mass adoption. That is optimistic commentary, but it leaves the outcome uncertain and does not assure viewers that they will earn money. The material therefore reads as a qualified opinion about a volatile market, with the viewer still responsible for deciding whether the information is useful.

citations.quote: The more big big players go towards crypto, the faster it goes towards the mass adaptation!
Every 1st and every 3. Tuesday of the month I present an exciting coin that has the potential in the next Bullrun.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The paid course and subscription do not themselves establish deception. The relevant investment language is expressly qualified as potential, not certainty, and the offer does not state that the coin will rise or that subscribers will receive a guaranteed return. Calling an uncertain forecast a scam would erase the distinction between speculative commentary and a promise of profit.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “Potential” is not a meaningful risk warning when viewers are asked to pay recurring access specifically to learn about a coin and build a portfolio with it. The offer connects the paid service to a future appreciation narrative; it need not guarantee success to solicit participation in a potentially misleading token opportunity.

Would you like to get to know this coin and build your portfolio with it?

opening.argument: The video's primary subject is a technology and market-news explanation: the speaker discusses an announced working relationship between PancakeSwap and Google Cloud and explains that Google Cloud is used to keep the platform available. The supplied frames show Google Cloud material describing platform availability and the speaker frames the development as another step in crypto's broader adoption. That is commentary on an industry event and infrastructure, not a demonstration that viewers should deposit funds or buy a particular asset.

citations.quote: PancakeSwap and Google are working together.
is using Google Cloud to keep the PancakeSwap platform open.
Another step in the adaptation of masses.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The description contains promotional material, but the spoken video and displayed material focus on the Google Cloud and PancakeSwap development. The speaker does not use the commentary to instruct viewers to transfer money, and the supplied frames depict platform infrastructure rather than a purchase screen or promised return. The news context is therefore central to what is actually presented.

citations.quote: Google, PancakeSwap, Google and cryptocurrencies, this is a very exciting partnership.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The infrastructure discussion is contextual, but it does not answer the description's direct paid offer. Viewers are invited to buy a course or pay monthly to receive a coin presentation, and are asked whether they want to use that coin to build a portfolio. News framing does not remove the investment solicitation attached to the content.

in order to only receive the coin.
Would you like to get to know this coin and build your portfolio with it?

opening.argument: The offer is described as ordinary paid education and subscription access: a cryptocurrency course for basic knowledge or a EUR 19.95 monthly subscription that can be canceled at any time. The supplied material does not show a required deposit, a guaranteed return, a downline-income scheme, or a request for credentials. It also does not establish that viewers must purchase a token from the creator. On the evidence provided, this is a conventional service promotion alongside crypto commentary, not a demonstrated scam mechanism.

citations.quote: Then now secure my new crypto course for the complete basic knowledge:
completing a subscription at EUR 19.95 per month (can be canceled at any time)
You can see everything else on Kryptoharry.com and get in touch with me.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The description identifies a paid service with a stated price and cancellation condition, which is ordinary commerce. A service may discuss coins without becoming a token-sale scheme. The record does not show money being deposited into a trading platform, credentials being collected, returns being promised, or recruitment being required, so the alleged mechanism is missing.

citations.quote: EUR 19.95 per month (can be canceled at any time)
PancakeSwap and Google are working together.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not merely that a course has a price. The paid subscription is offered so viewers can receive a recurring coin presentation, and the same offer asks whether they want to use that coin to build a portfolio. That links ordinary payment to speculative token participation even without a demonstrated deposit or guaranteed return.
